Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaRetail Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call to minimize background noise. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaRetail's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; and Lisa Wong, COO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen, CEO of NovaRetail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by exceptional active buyer count growth through effective user acquisition and retention, alongside impressive seller performance metrics including expansions in active sellers and revenue per seller. Our marketplace flywheel is accelerating, bolstered by robust mobile app engagement with surging downloads, active users, and conversion rates.

Our focus remains on scaling our ecosystem while enhancing user experiences across channels. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI-powered personalization tools, which we believe will significantly boost long-term customer lifetime value.

Finally, we are committed to delivering consistent GMV growth, both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, while exceeding guidance through disciplined execution in high-potential markets.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. Our Q3 revenue was $6.8 billion, an increase of 22% year-over-year. Gross margin was 42%, driven by improved supply chain efficiencies, take rate expansion, and a favorable category mix shift toward higher-margin goods. Operating expenses were $2.1 billion, representing 31% of revenue, reflecting disciplined investments in technology and marketing.

Our net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $1.45 per share. We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $28-30 billion in revenue and 18-20% GMV growth.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for NovaRetail. Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of our core growth engines: active buyer count expansion, with a specific focus on user acquisition and retention rates. For context, we define an active buyer as a unique customer who has made at least one purchase in the trailing 12 months—a standard metric across the e-commerce sector that aligns with peers like Amazon, Shopify-powered merchants, and Alibaba's ecosystem.

In Q3, our global active buyer base reached a record 152 million, marking a robust 24% year-over-year growth and 7% quarter-over-quarter increase. This outperforms the broader online retail industry's average of 15-18% YoY growth, as reported by eMarketer's latest benchmarks, and positions us ahead of direct comparables like Etsy at 12% YoY and Wayfair's flat growth amid housing market headwinds. Sequential acceleration from Q2's 22% YoY underscores the efficacy of our dual-pronged strategy: aggressive frontline acquisition paired with sophisticated retention levers. Let me break this down into acquisition dynamics, retention performance, regional nuances, and the technical and strategic initiatives driving these results.

We added 18.5 million net new active buyers in Q3, a 28% YoY increase from the 14.4 million added last year. This was fueled by a multi-channel Customer Acquisition Cost optimization playbook, where we maintained blended CAC at $28 per new buyer—down 12% YoY and well below the industry average of $35-40, per Gartner data for mid-tier e-commerce platforms.

Paid acquisition channels were the growth workhorse, accounting for 45% of new buyers. Google Ads and Meta platforms delivered scalable volume at sub-$25 CAC, while emerging channels like TikTok For Business contributed 15% of adds with viral coefficients above 1.2 in Gen Z cohorts. Organic channels, including SEO and app store optimization, drove 30% of growth, with our content hub generating 2x ROI versus paid. Retention efforts amplified this: Our churn rate dropped to 8% annualized, versus 12% industry average, through post-purchase nurturing sequences that lifted LTV by 18%.

Regionally, North America added 7.2 million net new buyers, up 25% YoY, powered by Prime-like subscription trials converting at 22%. APAC exploded with 6.8 million adds, a 38% surge, thanks to localized campaigns in India and Indonesia leveraging Jio and Grab partnerships. EMEA and LatAm contributed the balance, with 4.5 million combined, navigating regs via compliant data strategies.

Strategically, NovaAI's recommendation engine and loyalty gamification have been pivotal, with repeat buyer rates hitting 65%. Looking forward, we see 25%+ YoY buyer growth sustaining.

Moving now to our seller performance metrics, which remain a cornerstone of our marketplace flywheel here at NovaRetail. As you know, our platform thrives on a vibrant ecosystem of third-party sellers, who account for over 65% of our Gross Merchandise Value, or GMV, mirroring the model that's propelled leaders like Amazon and Alibaba to dominance. Today, I'll dive into our two key metrics: the number of active sellers—defined as those with at least one sale in the trailing 12 months—and revenue per seller, which we calculate on an annualized basis as total seller-generated revenue divided by active sellers.

Starting with active sellers: We're thrilled to report that we ended Q3 at 2.8 million active sellers globally, up a robust 28% year-over-year from 2.2 million in Q3 2023. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, accelerating from 22% in Q2. Sequentially, we added 180,000 net new active sellers, outpacing our guidance and reflecting strong onboarding momentum.

Breaking it down regionally, North America continues to lead with 1.1 million active sellers, up 25% YoY, fueled by our deepened integrations with Shopify merchants and small business tools like QuickBooks. In APAC, our fastest-growing region, we hit 950,000 active sellers—a stellar 42% YoY surge—driven by expansions into high-potential markets like Indonesia and India, where we've localized our seller dashboard for Bahasa and Hindi, and partnered with local payment gateways like GoPay and PhonePe to reduce friction. EMEA grew more modestly at 18% YoY to 550,000, tempered by regulatory headwinds around DSA compliance, but we're seeing green shoots in the UK and Germany post our VAT automation rollout. Latin America rounded out at 200,000, up 35% YoY, with Brazil's Pix integration proving a game-changer for micro-sellers.

On revenue per seller, we achieved an annualized $48,200 in Q3, representing a 14% YoY increase from $42,300 last year and up 4% sequentially. This metric is particularly telling of our seller monetization health—think of it as our marketplace equivalent of ARPU for SaaS platforms like Shopify. The uplift breaks down into two levers: a modest 2-point expansion in our blended take rate to 12.8% on seller services revenue including fulfillment, advertising, and premium subscriptions, and more importantly, a 10%+ improvement in seller velocity through organic GMV per seller growth.

What drove this? First, category mix shift: High-margin electronics and beauty categories, which grew 30% YoY in seller participation, now represent 28% of seller GMV versus 22% last year, echoing Etsy's premium handmade focus but at NovaRetail scale. Second, our AI-powered Seller Success Suite, launched in Q4 last year, has been a powerhouse—using machine learning models trained on 15 billion historical transactions to deliver personalized listing optimizations, dynamic pricing recommendations, and demand forecasting. Sellers using these tools saw 22% higher revenue per listing, with adoption now at 65% of actives, up from 40% a year ago.

We've also leaned into logistics tailwinds: Our NovaRetail Fulfillment Network, or NFN, now covers 85% of seller inventory with same-day delivery in top metros, reducing cart abandonment by 18% and boosting repeat orders. This is especially evident in APAC, where revenue per seller hit $55,000 annualized—20% above our global average—thanks to robotics-enabled warehouses in Singapore and Mumbai.

Strategically, these metrics underscore our "Seller-First Acceleration" initiative, a $250 million investment this fiscal year in three pillars: frictionless onboarding via API integrations with ERP systems like SAP and WooCommerce, slashing activation time from 14 days to 3; advanced analytics with tools like our new Seller Intelligence Hub, powered by generative AI akin to Amazon's Rufus, helping sellers predict trends in fast-fashion or consumer electronics; and global expansion plays, including a new seller accelerator program in Southeast Asia targeting 500,000 TikTok Shop migrants by year-end.

Looking ahead, we expect active sellers to grow 25-30% YoY in FY2024, with revenue per seller trending toward $52,000 by Q4, supported by take rate expansion to 13.5% and further AI tooling. Risks include macroeconomic pressures on consumer discretionary spend—our seller surveys show 15% citing softer demand—but our diversified base of 70% small-and-medium enterprises with under $1 million in annual sales provides resilience, much like Alibaba's Taobao ecosystem.

In summary, our seller metrics are firing on all cylinders, driving 32% YoY marketplace revenue growth to $4.2 billion this quarter. This positions NovaRetail to capture more of the $6.5 trillion global e-commerce TAM, as projected by eMarketer.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining NovaRetail's Q3 earnings call. As we continue to navigate a dynamic e-commerce landscape marked by macroeconomic headwinds, supply chain stabilization, and intensifying competition from pure-plays like Amazon and Shein, our mobile app remains a cornerstone of our omnichannel strategy. Mobile now accounts for 62% of our total GMV—up from 55% a year ago—underscoring its role in driving higher ARPU and customer LTV through superior engagement and conversion. Today, I'll dive deep into our mobile app performance across downloads, active users, and conversion rates, with key trends, regional insights, and the technical initiatives fueling our momentum.

Starting with downloads: We delivered an impressive 5.2 million new app downloads in Q3, representing 28% year-over-year growth and 12% quarter-over-quarter acceleration. This outpaces the broader app economy, where Sensor Tower data shows e-commerce app downloads growing at just 15% YoY globally. Android drove 68% of these, reflecting our aggressive push in high-growth emerging markets, while iOS contributed 32%, bolstered by our optimized App Store presence post-ATT framework adjustments.

Breaking it down regionally: North America led with 2.1 million downloads, up 22% YoY, fueled by targeted ASO campaigns around back-to-school and holiday pre-sales. APAC was the star, adding 1.8 million, up 45% YoY, particularly in Southeast Asia where we've localized the app for markets like Indonesia and Vietnam with Bahasa support and partnerships with Shopee-like local wallets. EMEA lagged slightly at 900,000, up 18% YoY, impacted by regulatory hurdles like GDPR cookie consents, but we're seeing early traction from our EU-specific sustainability features. Cohort analysis shows our Q3 download cohort retaining 35% higher than Q2, thanks to onboarding optimizations like personalized first-session recommendations.

Turning to active users: Our daily active users, or DAU, hit a record 4.8 million, up 20% YoY and 8% QoQ, while monthly active users, or MAU, reached 16.2 million, up 24% YoY. This translates to a sticky DAU/MAU ratio of 30%—well above the 22% industry benchmark per Appsflyer—indicating robust habit formation. Average session length climbed to 7.2 minutes, up 15% YoY, driven by immersive features we'll discuss shortly. Retention metrics are equally strong: Day 7 retention at 42% versus 35% industry average for retail apps, Day 30 at 28%, and Day 90 at 18%. Push notification opt-in rates stand at 72%, enabling 3x higher re-engagement versus non-opted users.

Regionally, NA remains our powerhouse with 2.2 million DAU, 45% of total, where urban millennials drive 60% of sessions via quick-reorder functionalities akin to Amazon's 'Buy Again.' APAC's 1.5 million DAU, up 35% YoY, highlights viral growth in India, where UPI integration has boosted repeat usage amid JioMart competition. EMEA's 900,000 DAU grew 15% YoY but faces headwinds from economic slowdowns in the UK and Germany; however, our cohort LTV here is 25% above web-only users due to app-exclusive loyalty perks.

Now, conversion rates—the true north star for monetization: App conversion from session to purchase soared to 9.2% in Q3, up 180 basis points YoY and 60 bps QoQ, decisively outperforming our mobile web at 4.8% and desktop at 3.9%. This gap is widening, with app AOV 22% higher at $68 versus $56 on web, thanks to upsell carousels and dynamic bundling. Add-to-cart abandonment dropped to 22% from 28% YoY, largely from one-tap checkout flows.

Key trends here include a post-ATT recovery: After iOS 14.5's impact shaved 15% off our prior attribution, we've clawed back via server-side tracking and SKAdNetwork 4.0 compliance, restoring 85% of pre-ATT accuracy. Android conversions hit 10.1% in APAC, leveraging cheaper CAC at $2.50 versus $5.80 iOS and features like AR virtual try-on for fashion SKUs, which boosted apparel conversions by 32%. A slight Q3 dip in NA electronics down 50 bps tied to tariff uncertainties on China-sourced goods, but we've offset this with app-only flash sales mimicking Temu's model.

Underpinning this performance are targeted technical initiatives: We've rolled out GenAI-powered personalization via our proprietary 'NovaRec' engine—similar to Stitch Fix's algo but scaled for 10 million+ users—delivering 25% uplift in click-through rates on home feeds. In-app experiences now include AR try-on live for 40% of fashion inventory, up 18% conversion; social commerce via Instagram Shop integrations; and gamified loyalty with 'Spin-to-Win' wheels yielding 14% higher redemption rates. We've A/B tested 47 variants on checkout friction, cutting steps from 8 to 4, and integrated Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna BNPL universally—BNPL now 28% of app transactions. Backend-wise, our shift to Flutter for cross-platform development reduced update cycles by 40%, enabling faster feature ships like voice search optimized for Hindi/Spanish.

Strategically, these metrics position us for outsized growth: Mobile app engagement directly correlates to a 35% higher LTV at $420 versus $310 web and 22% lower CAC, giving us a durable moat against discounters like Wish. We're allocating $45 million in FY25 capex to app R&D, including Web3 wallet pilots for NFT loyalty drops and edge computing for sub-100ms load times in LatAm expansions. Projections: Q4 DAU up 15% QoQ, conversions to 9.8%, targeting 20% of GMV from app-exclusive deals.

In summary, our app is not just a channel—it's our growth engine in a $6.5 trillion global e-commerce market projected to hit 25% CAGR through 2028 per Statista.

Thank you, Sarah. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us on NovaRetail's Q3 2024 earnings call. I'll dive right into our top-line performance, starting with Gross Merchandise Value, or GMV, which remains the cornerstone metric for our marketplace ecosystem. As a reminder, GMV represents the total value of goods sold through our platform by our third-party sellers and first-party fulfillment, excluding returns and refunds.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2024, we delivered total GMV of $25.4 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 12th straight quarter of accelerating YoY GMV growth and comfortably exceeded our guidance range of 15-17% YoY, which we laid out during our Q2 call. On a QoQ basis, we also beat our implied sequential growth target of 3-5%, reflecting resilient consumer demand amid moderating inflation and a choppy macro environment.

Let me unpack the drivers here, as this performance underscores the strength of our flywheel: more active buyers, higher engagement, and sticky monetization.

Year-over-Year Breakdown: YoY GMV growth of 18% was fueled by a 22% increase in our Monthly Active Buyers to 185 million globally, outpacing the broader e-commerce industry average of ~12% as reported by eMarketer. This was driven by our hyper-personalized recommendation engine, powered by our proprietary NovaAI model—similar to Amazon's Rufus but optimized for cross-category discovery—which boosted conversion rates by 15% in A/B tests. Average Order Value grew 4% YoY to $145, benefiting from upselling in high-margin categories like electronics and premium beauty, where we saw 25% category GMV growth. We leaned into this with targeted bundles, akin to Shopify's dynamic bundling tools. Orders per active buyer rose 3%, thanks to our loyalty program enhancements, including Nova Prime's expanded perks like same-day delivery in 80% of urban U.S. markets via our partnership with DoorDash.

Quarter-over-Quarter Dynamics: Sequential GMV growth of 5% was solid, especially against a tough comp from Q2's back-to-school surge. Excluding seasonal factors, underlying growth was ~7%, aligning with peers like Etsy and Wayfair, who reported 4-6% QoQ in their recent prints. MABs grew 3% QoQ, with particular strength in emerging markets. AOV held steady sequentially, as we balanced promotional activity—our sitewide discounts averaged 18% off RRP—to drive traffic without eroding margins.

Regional Commentary: North America, 65% of GMV, delivered 20% YoY growth to $16.5 billion, beating our 17-19% guide. U.S. consumers shifted toward value-driven purchases amid 3.2% CPI cooling, with our private-label 'Nova Essentials' line—competing directly with Walmart+ and Amazon Basics—capturing 15% share in groceries and household goods. APAC, 20% of GMV, explosive 28% YoY growth to $5.1 billion, led by India and Southeast Asia. Our investments in vernacular search and UPI integrations mirrored Flipkart's playbook, driving 35% MAB growth in India alone. TikTok Shop-like social commerce features added $800 million in incremental GMV. EMEA, 12% of GMV, moderated to 12% YoY growth at $3.0 billion, impacted by the EU's Digital Markets Act enforcement and VAT headwinds, similar to what Zalando flagged last quarter. We mitigated this with localized pricing algorithms, maintaining take rates above 22%. Rest of World, 3%, 25% YoY growth, with early traction in Latin America via Mercado Libre-inspired seller onboarding tools.

Technical Initiatives and Strategic Insights: This outperformance wasn't accidental—it's the payoff from our 'Nova Next' tech roadmap. We rolled out full-stack machine learning for demand forecasting, reducing stockouts by 30% and enabling just-in-time inventory like Alibaba's Cainiao network. Our cloud-native logistics backbone, now handling 1.2 billion parcels annually, cut delivery times to under 48 hours in key hubs, lifting repeat purchase rates by 8%.

Strategically, we're doubling down on high-growth vectors: social commerce now 15% of GMV up from 10% YoY, live-streaming partnerships with influencers driving 40% higher AOV, and B2B wholesale via our NovaPro portal, which contributed $2.5 billion in GMV. Against competitive pressures from low-cost disruptors like Temu and Shein—who flooded the market with $50B+ in U.S. GMV last year per Insider Intelligence—we've fortified our moat with exclusive brand deals like Nike direct integration and sustainability filters, resonating with 60% of Gen Z shoppers per our surveys.

Looking ahead, for Q4, we're guiding GMV growth of 17-19% YoY, implying $28-29 billion, with sequential growth of 6-8%. This assumes stable consumer sentiment but hedges against potential tariff escalations on Chinese imports. We're well-positioned with $4.2 billion in cash and a 25% take rate expansion runway.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter:
Thanks for taking my question. Sarah, could you expand on the active buyer growth drivers, particularly how retention is holding up in a tougher macro environment, and any updates on CAC trends?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Emily. Absolutely, our 24% YoY active buyer growth to 152 million is a testament to our balanced acquisition and retention strategy. We added 18.5 million net new buyers at a blended CAC of just $28, down 12% YoY, thanks to optimized paid channels like Google and Meta making up 45% of adds. Retention is strong, with churn at 8% annualized, driven by NovaAI personalization lifting repeat rates to 65%. Even with macro pressures, our regional focus—strong APAC adds via local partnerships—keeps us resilient. We're confident in sustaining 25% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with Morgan Stanley.

Raj Singh:
Hi, team. Mike, great GMV beat—can you talk more about the regional breakdowns and how you're thinking about take rate expansion amid competition from Temu and Shein?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, Raj. Our $25.4 billion GMV grew 18% YoY, beating 15-17% guidance, with NA at 20% to $16.5 billion on value shifts to Nova Essentials, APAC exploding 28% to $5.1 billion via UPI and social features, and EMEA at 12% navigating regs. Take rates are expanding to 12.8% globally, with runway to 13.5% via AI tools in Seller Success Suite, where adoption hit 65%. Against Temu/Shein, our moat is in exclusive brands like Nike and 85% NFN coverage reducing abandonment—positioning us for Q4 17-19% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
Thanks. Lisa, on mobile app metrics, impressive DAU and conversions—how are you sustaining that stickiness, and any color on APAC specifics versus NA?

Lisa Wong:
David, thanks. Our app drove 62% of GMV, with 5.2 million downloads up 28% YoY, DAU at 4.8 million up 20%, and conversions at 9.2% up 180 bps. Stickiness from 30% DAU/MAU, 7.2-min sessions, and D7 retention at 42% via NovaRec GenAI (25% CTR lift), AR try-on, and BNPL at 28% of txns. APAC shines with 1.5 million DAU up 35%, 10.1% Android conversions from UPI and cheaper CAC; NA's 2.2 million DAU leverages quick-reorder for 22% higher AOV. $45 million FY25 capex will push Q4 DAU 15% QoQ.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
